source: NCERT Class VI, Curiosity: Textbook of Science, Ch. 11.

sections.heading: 1. Nature's Treasures — Natural Resources
points: **Natural resources** = useful things we get **from nature**: **air, water, soil, minerals, forests, wildlife, sunlight**.

sub: **Renewable** — can be replaced/renewed in a reasonable time (sunlight, air, water, forests, wind).
**Non-renewable** — limited and take millions of years to form; can get exhausted (**coal, petroleum, natural gas, minerals**).

points: Resources must be used wisely and **conserved**.

sections.heading: 2. Air
points: Air is a **mixture of gases**: roughly **78% nitrogen, 21% oxygen**, and small amounts of carbon dioxide, argon and water vapour.
**Oxygen** supports breathing and burning; **carbon dioxide** is used by plants in photosynthesis.
Air also provides **wind energy**.

sections.heading: 3. Water and Soil
points: **Water:** only a **small fraction** of Earth's water is usable **fresh water**; most is salty ocean water. Sources: rivers, lakes, groundwater, rain.
**Soil:** the top layer of land supporting plants; formed by the **weathering of rocks** over long periods; holds water, air and nutrients.
Both must be protected from **pollution and overuse**.

sections.heading: 4. Fossil Fuels and Minerals
points: **Fossil fuels** — **coal, petroleum (crude oil), natural gas** — formed from remains of ancient plants/animals over **millions of years**; **non-renewable**.
**Minerals** (iron, copper, aluminium, etc.) are dug from the Earth and are also **exhaustible**.
Burning fossil fuels causes **pollution** → we should use **renewable energy** (solar, wind, hydro).

sections.heading: 5. Conservation
points: **Conserve** resources by the **3 R's: Reduce, Reuse, Recycle**.
Save water and electricity; plant trees; prevent pollution; use public transport.
Uneven **distribution** of resources means some regions have plenty and others little — sharing and wise use matter.

sections.heading: 6. High-Yield One-Liners (Last-Minute Recall)
points: Natural resources: renewable (sun, air, water, forests) vs non-renewable (coal, petroleum, natural gas, minerals).
Air ≈ 78% nitrogen, 21% oxygen (+ CO₂, argon, water vapour).
Fossil fuels = coal, petroleum, natural gas — non-renewable, formed over millions of years.
Soil forms by weathering of rocks; only a little of Earth's water is usable fresh water.
Conserve with the 3 R's: Reduce, Reuse, Recycle.

sections.heading: 7. Common Traps (Watch Out)
points: **Coal, petroleum and natural gas are NON-renewable** (fossil fuels) — they will run out.
Air is about **78% nitrogen and 21% oxygen** — nitrogen is the most abundant gas.
**Renewable** resources can be replenished (sun, wind, water); non-renewable cannot in our lifetime.
Most of Earth's water is **salty**; usable fresh water is a small fraction.
